Rashi on Niddah 8b:10:1.english: For a High Priest - As he is commanded to marry a virgin.

Rashi on Niddah 8b:10:2.english: For her marriage contract [to be] two hundred - For if she has engaged in intercourse, she is no longer called a virgin, and her marriage contract is a maneh [one hundred dinars].

Rashi on Niddah 8b:11:1.hebrew: למקח וממכר - שאם אמר לו קרקע בתולה אני מוכר לך, נותן לו קרקע שלא נעבדה, לפי שעושה פירות מרובין ושמנים:
Rashi on Niddah 8b:11:1.english: With regard to buying and selling - That if [a seller] said to [a buyer]: "I am selling you virgin land," he must give him land that has not been worked, because it produces abundant and rich fruit.

Rashi on Niddah 8b:12:1.hebrew: שלא נקצצה - כן מנהג לקוצצה, כדי שירבה עוביו ויוציא ענפים הרבה במקום החתך, ונקרא סדן שקמה:
Rashi on Niddah 8b:12:1.english: That has not been cut - Such is the practice, to cut it so that its thickness will increase and it will put forth many branches at the site of the cut, and it is [then] called a sycamore trunk.

Rashi on Niddah 8b:12:2.hebrew: למקח וממכר - לפי שנוח לו בבתולה, שילדה היא, ויקצצנה ומתעבה:
Rashi on Niddah 8b:12:2.english: For buying and selling - Because a virgin [sycamore] is preferable to him, as it is young, and he will cut it and it will thicken.

Rashi on Niddah 8b:12:3.english: Let him also teach this - And let him say: "There are four virgins."

Rashi on Niddah 8b:13:1.hebrew: שם לווי - כגון בתולה דמתניתין, לאו בתולה סתם מיקריא, אלא בתולת דמים, דסתם בתולה בנשים היינו בתולת בתולים. וכן קרקע בתולה, וכן שקמה בתולה, לא בעי שם לווי:
Rashi on Niddah 8b:13:1.english: A modifier - For example, the virgin of our mishna is not called simply "a virgin," but rather "a virgin of blood," for an unqualified "virgin" among women is a virgin of virginity [i.e., with an intact hymen]. And similarly, virgin land and a virgin sycamore do not require a modifier.

Rashi on Niddah 8b:13:2.hebrew: דתלי במעשה - שאינו מאבד שמו אלא ע"י מעשה, אבל ראיית דם מאיליה באה ואבדה שם בתולה:
Rashi on Niddah 8b:13:2.english: That depends on an action - Which does not lose its designation except through an action, but the appearance of blood comes on its own, and she loses the designation of virgin.

Rashi on Niddah 8b:14:1.english: That returns to its original state - Such as an elderly woman whose [menstrual] blood ceases.

Rashi on Niddah 8b:14:2.hebrew: דקפיד עליה זבינא - נותן עיניו בכך, כגון בתולה נוחה לינשא מבעולה, וכן קרקע ושקמה. אבל בתולת דמים, אין אדם נותן עיניו בדמים, דלא חייש אי חזיא אי לא חזיא:
Rashi on Niddah 8b:14:2.english: That a buyer is particular about it - [He] pays attention to this: for example, a virgin is more readily married than a non-virgin, and likewise land and a sycamore. But [regarding] a virgin with respect to blood, a person does not pay attention to [menstrual] blood, as he does not care whether she sees [blood] or does not see [it].

Rashi on Niddah 8b:15:1.hebrew: דקפיץ עליה - שנוחה בתולה ללקוחות, כגון בתולת בתולים וקרקע ושקמה; אבל בתולת דמים, כל כמה דחזיא ניחא ליה טפי, כדאמרינן:
Rashi on Niddah 8b:15:1.english: That [a buyer] leaps at it - That a virgin is preferable to buyers, such as a virgin of virginity [i.e., a woman who has not had intercourse], and [virgin] land, and a [virgin] sycamore; but as for a virgin of blood, the more [blood] she has seen, the more pleasing it is to him, as we said.

Rashi on Niddah 8b:16:1.hebrew: רשושין - אבנים דקין, שקורין פרדוי"א. לשון אחר: רגבי אדמה קשין, שאין עפרם מתפזר:
Rashi on Niddah 8b:16:1.english: Hard clumps - Fine stones, which are called *pedruge* [gravel]. Another explanation: Hard clods of earth whose soil does not scatter.

Rashi on Niddah 8b:16:3.hebrew: בידוע שנעבדה - דאי לא נעבדה, חרס זה מאין בא לתוכה:
Rashi on Niddah 8b:16:3.english: It is known that it was worked - For if it had not been worked, from where did this earthenware shard come into it?

Rashi on Niddah 8b:18:1.hebrew: דילדה לז' - שמא ניכר עוברה לשליש ימיה, דהיינו שני חדשים ושליש, קמ"ל דאזלינן בתר רוב נשים:
Rashi on Niddah 8b:18:1.english: Who gives birth at seven - [Lest one think that] perhaps her fetus is recognizable at one-third of her term, which is two months and a third, it comes to teach us that we follow the majority of women.

Rashi on Niddah 8b:19:1.hebrew: דיה שעתה - לא אמרינן איגלאי מילתא למפרע דלאו הריון הוא, ונטמאו טהרות דמעת לעת של ראיה:
Rashi on Niddah 8b:19:1.english: Her time is sufficient - We do not say that the matter has been revealed retroactively, that it was not a pregnancy, and [that] the ritually pure items of the twenty-four hours prior to the sighting became impure.

Rashi on Niddah 8b:1:1.hebrew: והא קשיש מיניה טובא - דהא ר' אליעזר היה בימי ר"ג, בנו של ר"ש הנהרג בהרוגי מלכות, ובעל אחותו היה, כדאמרי' בהזהב (ב"מ דף נט:). ור' חנינא בנו של ר"ג היה:
Rashi on Niddah 8b:1:1.english: But wasn't he much older than him - For Rabbi Eliezer lived in the days of Rabban Gamliel, son of Rabban Shimon who was killed among the martyrs of the regime, and [Rabbi Eliezer] was the husband of his sister, as we say in [chapter] HaZahav (Bava Metzia 59b). And Rabbi Chanina was the son of Rabban Gamliel.

Rashi on Niddah 8b:20:1.english: An allusion to the matter - That a pregnancy of wind is called a pregnancy.

Rashi on Niddah 8b:21:1.hebrew: קשתה שני ימים - בתוך אחד עשר ימי זוב, ולשלישי נמי ראתה, ואח"כ הפילה רוח בו ביום, ולא שפתה מן הצער, הרי לידה זו בזוב, וצריכה שבעה נקיים וקרבן לזיבתה, דכיון דלאו ולד הוא, הויא זיבה מעליא:
Rashi on Niddah 8b:21:1.english: She experienced hard labor for two days - [This occurred] within the eleven days of zivah, and on the third [day] she also saw [blood], and afterward she miscarried wind on that [same] day, and she had not found relief from the pain; behold, this is childbirth in [a state of] zivah, and she requires seven clean [days] and an offering for her zivah, for since it is not a child, it is a full-fledged zivah.

Rashi on Niddah 8b:2:1.english: Light - The night of its onset.

Rashi on Niddah 8b:2:2.hebrew: מעין שמנה עשרה - שאומר בשבעה ברכות מעין שמונה עשרה, כגון ג' ראשונות וג' אחרונות כתקנן, ואומר הביננו באמצע ומסיים בשומע תפלה, כדאמרינן בברכות (דף כט.), ויש בה מעין כולם:
Rashi on Niddah 8b:2:2.english: An abridgment of the eighteen - That one recites an abridgment of the eighteen in seven blessings, such as the first three and last three [blessings] in their standard form, and one recites Havineinu in the middle and concludes with "Who hears prayer," as we say in Berakhot (page 29a); and it contains an abridgment of all of them.

Rashi on Niddah 8b:4:1.english: One who curdles - [Curdling] animal milk to make cheese.

Rashi on Niddah 8b:5:1.hebrew: בקטפא דגווזא - בשרף הנוטף מן העץ, דכעץ בעלמא הוי. אבל קטף הוי שרף הפגין, ומודו בהו רבנן:
Rashi on Niddah 8b:5:1.english: In the sap of the tree - In the sap that drips from the tree, for it is merely like wood. But *kataf* is the sap of unripe figs, and the Rabbis concede regarding them.

Rashi on Niddah 8b:7:1.hebrew: לאו רבנן דפליגי עליה דר"א - בשאר אילנות, וחזינן דבקטף סבירא להו כוותיה:
Rashi on Niddah 8b:7:1.english: Are they not the Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Eliezer - With regard to other trees, and we see that with regard to sap they hold in accordance with him.

Rashi on Niddah 8b:9:1.hebrew: בתולת דמים - דמי נדה ולא דמי בתולים, דאפילו נבעלה עדיין היא בתולת דמים:
Rashi on Niddah 8b:9:1.english: A virgin with respect to blood - [Meaning] menstrual blood and not hymeneal blood, for even if she engaged in intercourse, she is still a virgin with respect to blood.

Tosafot on Niddah 8b:1:1.hebrew: והא קשיש מיניה טובא - ר"א מרבי חנינא. פרש"י, שר' חנינא היה בנו של ר"ג דיבנה. וכ"נ, דבפרק המפלת (לקמן נדה דף כג.) א"ר חנינא בן גמליאל: נראין דברי ר"מ בבהמה ובחיה. וא"ת: והא בת"כ (פ' אמור), גבי פנחס איש הסתת שעלה גורלו להיות כ"ג כו', אמר ר' חנינא בן רבן גמליאל: וכי סתת היה? והלא חתנינו היה, וחורש היה! ואי בן ר"ג דיבנה היה, היאך היה לו חתן כ"ג? והלא היה אחר החורבן! וי"ל, דלאו חתנינו ממש קאמר, אלא חתן אבותיו; וכן משמע, דלא אמר חתני, אלא חתנינו היה:
Tosafot on Niddah 8b:1:1.english: But wasn't he much older than him - [Namely,] Rabbi Eliezer [was older] than Rabbi Ḥanina. Rashi explained that Rabbi Ḥanina was the son of Rabban Gamliel of Yavneh. And so it appears, as in the chapter [entitled] "HaMapyelet" (below, Niddah 23a), Rabbi Ḥanina ben Gamliel said: "The words of Rabbi Meir appear [correct] regarding a domesticated animal and a wild animal." And if you say: But in Torat Kohanim (Parashat Emor), regarding Pineḥas the stonecutter whose lot came up to be High Priest, etc., Rabbi Ḥanina ben Rabban Gamliel said: "Was he [really] a stonecutter? Was he not our son-in-law, and he was a plowman!" And if he was the son of Rabban Gamliel of Yavneh, how could he have had a son-in-law who was a High Priest? Was he not [living] after the Destruction! And one can say that he did not mean our literal son-in-law, but rather a son-in-law of his ancestors. And so it is implied [by the phrasing], as he did not say "my son-in-law" (ḥatani), but rather "he was our son-in-law" (ḥatanenu).

Tosafot on Niddah 8b:2:1.hebrew: [ומאי קאי – הר"מ ז"ל אמר, דלא פריך מברייתא אברייתא, משום דה"א דהדר ביה מההיא דהודאה (אחרינא שמע) מרבותיו; אבל השתא דקאמר דקאי בשיטתיה, משמע דלא הדר ביה, דאל"כ, אכתי תיקשי: ותו ליכא? לכך פריך שפיר: ומאי קאי. גי']:
Tosafot on Niddah 8b:2:1.english: [And what is "he holds" - Harav Meir, of blessed memory, said that [the Gemara] did not object from [one] baraita against [the other] baraita, because we would have said that he retracted from that concession (he heard another [tradition]) from his teachers. But now that [the Gemara] says that he holds in accordance with his opinion, this implies that he did not retract; for if not so, it would still be difficult: "And are there no more?" Therefore, [the Gemara] rightly asks: "And what is 'he holds'?" – variant reading]:

Tosafot on Niddah 8b:3:1.hebrew: מפני שצריך לומר הבדלה בחונן הדעת - הקשה הר"ר יעקב מאורלינ"ש: ונכלליה מכלל! דהכי פריך פרק תפלת השחר (ברכות דף כט.) אהא דאמר שמואל: כל השנה מתפלל הביננו, חוץ ממוצאי שבת, מפני שצ"ל הבדלה בחונן הדעת; ופריך: ונכלליה מכלל! וי"ל, דהתם פריך משום דלא ישנה אדם משום הבדלה מכמו שהוא מתפלל כל השנה [כיון דסבר דכל השנה מתפלל הביננו], אלא יכלול בהביננו. והכא קאמר ר' חנינא: [כיון דס"ל דכל השנה אינו מתפלל הביננו, א"כ] במוצאי יוה"כ, מפני טורח תענית לא ישנה מכמו שהוא מתפלל כל השנה, כדי שיאמר הבדלה בחונן הדעת:
Tosafot on Niddah 8b:3:1.english: Because he must say Havdalah in "Chonen HaDa'at" - Rabbi Yaakov of Orléans raised a difficulty: But let him include it within [Havineinu]! For so [the Gemara] asks in the chapter [entitled] Tefillat HaShachar (Berakhot 29a) regarding that which Shmuel said: "All year round, one prays Havineinu, except for the conclusion of Shabbat, because he must say Havdalah in 'Chonen HaDa'at'"; and it asks: "And let him include it within [Havineinu]!" And one can say: There, it asks [this] because a person should not change, on account of Havdalah, from how he prays all year round [since he holds that all year round one prays Havineinu]; rather, he should include [it] within Havineinu. But here, Rabbi Chanina is saying: [Since he holds that all year round one does not pray Havineinu, if so,] on the conclusion of Yom Kippur, [even] due to the hardship of the fast, he should not change from how he prays all year round, so that he may say Havdalah in "Chonen HaDa'at".

Tosafot on Niddah 8b:5:1.hebrew: בקטפא דפירא מודו ליה דתנן א"ר יהושע כו' - וא"ת, [א"כ] אמאי אוקי רבי פדת מתניתין כר"א, כיון דרבנן מודו בקטפא דפירא? ואי משום דבעי לאוקומי בכל מיני קטף, אפי' בדגווזא — מ"מ היכי קאמר ליה ר' זירא: "חזי דמשתריא קטפא לעלמא"? הא ודאי אמת הוא דקטפא דגווזא שרי, דאף ר' זירא מודה דאין הלכה כר"א אלא בד'. וליכא למימר דאתי למטעי ולמשרי אף קטפא דפירא, מדלא מוקי רבי פדת מתני' בקטפא דפירא ודברי הכל, מכלל דסבר אף בקטפא דפירא רבנן הוא דשרו — הא לא אתי למטעי, דהא חזינן במשנה שאוסר רבי יהושע שרף הפגים. וי"ל, שיטעו ויסברו שרבי יהושע "שמעתי" קאמר, וליה לא ס"ל, מדלא מוקי ר' פדת מתני' כוותיה ובקטפא דפירא. ואפשר דר' פדת סבר דקטפא דפירא שרי, ור' [יהושע] קאמר "שמעתי", וליה לא סבירא ליה:
Tosafot on Niddah 8b:5:1.english: In [the case of] the sap of the fruit they agree with him, as we learned: Rabbi Yehoshua said, etc. - And if you say: [If so,] why did Rabbi Pedat establish our mishna in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer, since the Rabbis agree in [the case of] the sap of the fruit? And if [you say that it is] because he wanted to establish [it] with regard to all types of sap, even [the sap] of the wood (qitfa degavza) — nevertheless, how could Rabbi Zeira say to him: "See that sap is being permitted to the world"? Behold, it is certainly true that the sap of wood is permitted, for even Rabbi Zeira admits that the halakha is not in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer except in four [cases]! And one cannot say that [people] might come to err and permit even the sap of fruit, [reasoning that] since Rabbi Pedat did not establish the mishna as [referring to] the sap of fruit and [thus as being] unanimous (divrei hakol), by implication he holds that even in [the case of] the sap of fruit it is the Rabbis who permit [it] — for they would not come to err [in this way], as behold, we see in the mishna that Rabbi Yehoshua prohibits the sap of unripe figs! And one can say: [They were concerned] that they would err and think that Rabbi Yehoshua [merely] said "I have heard," but he himself does not hold [so], since Rabbi Pedat did not establish the mishna in accordance with his view and as [referring to] the sap of fruit. And it is possible that Rabbi Pedat [himself] held that the sap of fruit is permitted, and Rabbi [Yehoshua] said "I have heard," but he himself did not hold [accordingly].

Tosafot on Niddah 8b:7:1.hebrew: מאן חכמים (א"ר יוחנן) ר"א - אע"ג דתנא בלשון חכמים, ניחא ליה לאוקומי כר"א, ולא לימא ג' מחלוקות בדבר:
Tosafot on Niddah 8b:7:1.english: Who are the Sages? (Rabbi Yoḥanan said:) Rabbi Eliezer - Even though [the mishna] taught [it] in the language of "the Sages", he [Rabbi Yoḥanan] prefers to establish it as [the view of] Rabbi Eliezer, rather than say [that there are] three [differing] opinions on the matter.
